summary: Market sentiment is cautiously optimistic as equities attempt consecutive daily gains, though a complex web of geopolitical and macroeconomic pressures is keeping investors on edge. Surging diesel prices are prompting U.S. energy officials to push refiners for higher output, while elevated fuel costs have already forced United Airlines to slash its 2026 profit outlook, signaling that energy inflation is beginning to bite corporate earnings even as consumer travel demand remains resilient. The AI trade continues to dominate equity conversations, with traders booking profits in select AI names and rotating toward overlooked opportunities beyond CoreWeave, while Boeing's long-awaited FAA approval for the 737 Max 10 provided a discrete lift to the aerospace sector and Netflix options activity suggests traders anticipate a near-term resolution to the stock's recent volatility. The primary risk factors commanding investor attention include escalating Middle East tensions — Iran refusing talks with Washington, ongoing Gaza violence, and Britain deploying defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia — alongside U.S.-China tech friction over the proposed DeepSeek ban, all of which threaten to keep energy markets volatile and disrupt global supply chains. In the short term, markets are likely to remain range-bound, with any further geopolitical deterioration in the Middle East or a breakdown in U.S.-China relations capable of reversing fragile equity gains, while fuel cost pressures on transportation and consumer discretionary sectors will be closely scrutinized in upcoming earnings guidance.
